songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line

ai_show_review.summary: Estimated/Eyes jam, Touch of Grey and soaring Morning Dew
ai_show_review.blurb: The Frost Amphitheatre show delivers a monster Estimated Prophet → Eyes Of The World sequence and a fiery Touch of Grey that drives the second set. Jerry’s guitar soars while Phil lays down a “bomb” bass foundation, and Brent’s keys weave through the jams. Overall the performance is high‑energy with tight segues and a memorable Morning Dew finale.
ai_show_review.review: What unfolds at Frost Amphitheatre on October 9 1982 is a quintessential early‑80s Dead outing that balances crisp songcraft with expansive improvisation. The first set kicks off strong with Alabama Getaway and builds through an inspired On The Road Again → Beat It on Down the Line pairing, but it’s the second half that truly shines: Throwing Stones segues into Touch of Grey before launching into a blistering Estimated Prophet → Eyes Of The World stretch where Phil’s “bomb” bass and Jerry’s emotive leads lock in perfectly. The space‑drums excursion feeds into a tight Truckin' → The Other One → Morning Dew cascade, culminating in a soaring, almost transcendent rendition of Dew that feels both urgent and reflective. The encore U.S. Blues caps the night with classic Dead fire. Across the best soundboard source (the Miller SBD) the mix is crystal‑clear, delivering deep drums, pure guitar tone and balanced keyboards, letting every nuance of this high‑energy performance shine.

best_recording.reason: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture with deep drums, pure guitar tone and no reported dropouts – the most complete and sonically satisfying version.

key_highlights: Monster Estimated Prophet → Eyes Of The World jam with “bomb” bass and soaring leads
Electric Touch of Grey that drives the second set into a tight groove
Explosive The Other One → Morning Dew sequence delivering emotional climax
Overall high‑energy performance captured in an excellent soundboard mix

band_performance.Jerry: Delivers emotional, powerful leads throughout; guitar tone described as pure and gritty, with standout solos on Estimated/Eyes and soaring work on Morning Dew.
band_performance.Phil: Provides a “bomb” bass foundation that drives the jams, especially during Estimated Prophet → Eyes; noted for smiling onstage and energizing the crowd.
band_performance.Bob: While missing from some mixes, his rhythm guitar is front‑and‑center in audience recordings and adds quirky vocal interjections that spice up transitions like On The Road Again.
band_performance.Brent: Keyboard work is solid and intertwines well with the guitars; despite occasional criticism of a weak CP70 tone on some tapes, overall contributes essential texture to the improvisations.
band_performance.Mickey: Alongside Bill, offers propulsive, deep drum work that anchors the Space/Drums segment and fuels the high‑energy flow of the second set.
band_performance.Billy: Delivers tight, resonant drumming that complements Mickey; together they keep the rhythmic momentum steady through extended jams.
